newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends slightly weaker, fund selling seen.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends slightly weaker, fund selling seen.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended a shade weaker Friday, hit by carry-over speculative selling following the market's fall to three-week lows, trading sources said.
Selling pressure was heavy from both commodity funds and producer countries, with top-grower Ivory Coast leading the charge since its marketing season was officially opened on Thursday.
But bargain hunting by manufacturers, coupled with currency-linked arbitrage amid the British pound's advance, helped to stem the losses, traders said.
Traders said the market's steep fall on Thursday, highlighted by a drop in London to seven-month lows, weighed on the market's outlook at the start of the new crop year.
"Scale-down trade buying isn't going to be enough to support the market," commented one trader.

Benchmark December futures fell $2 on the day, to $1,360, its lowest settlement in three weeks, having traded from $1,357 to $1,371. Second-position March was down $1, to $1,389, while the outer months settled unchanged to down $7.
Volume on the day was fairly brisk, at 9,873 lots.
